notes: TARGET R34 addresses identifier consistency rule. PRIMARY evidence (E1) establishes that rent records receive unique identifiers. CONTEXT evidence reveals significant gaps: E4 and E5 document unresolved tension between business-defined item identifiers and warehouse/implementation identifiers; E8 raises audit visibility concerns about identifier representation. E6 specifies item ID format (8-char alphanumeric) but does not resolve the business-vs-operational identifier conflict. The requirement title suggests a consistency rule should exist, but the evidence shows active disagreement about which identifier representation should be authoritative. No PRIMARY evidence directly addresses the consistency rule itself; E1 only confirms unique assignment. Promotion of consistency rules to operative context is blocked by gaps in source-of-truth definition. Filtered abstract or low-relevance operative statements: System shall assign unique identifiers to rent records (E1: 2.1.5) | System shall assign unique identifiers to item records as 8-character alphanumeric strings (E6: 3.1.3) | System shall store timestamp and user identifier for each lifecycle event (E2: 2.8.3)
